caption:
We had no idea there were this many family-friendly activities available at Blue Mountain. Here’s a list of everything we did on our 3-day visit:
.
STAY:
We had a 2 bedroom suite in the Weider Lodge, which is located right at the base of the mountain. The gondola was right outside our door and it was a quick, easy walk to tons of restaurants, activities and shopping in Blue Mountain Village. The suite also had a full kitchen.
.
THINGS TO DO:
We had a full access pass which gave us entry to all of these activities:
☀️ Ridge Runner Mountain Coaster - this is a must-do when you’re at Blue Mountain!
☀️Plunge! Aquatic Centre - indoor/outdoor pool that is mostly shallow so kids can swim on their own. There’s also a toddler splash area, waterslide and a deep pool with a rope swing (swim test required for the deep pool)
☀️Adventure Park - Jump and climb on giant colourful trampolines in Cocoon Crawl, play on the giant wooden/rope playground in Canopy Climb and have fun with the giant marble runs at Chutes and Loops Ball Run
☀️ Open-Air Gondola - take a quick ride to the top of the mountain for incredible views 
☀️ Nature Trails - we did the “Cascade” trail, which took about 45 minutes and wound alongside a creek and waterfalls the whole way!
☀️ Blue Mountain Private Beach - lots of lounge chairs, change rooms, bathrooms and concession stand available
☀️ Kayaking - Kayaks and paddle boards are included with your visit to the private beach!
‼️ Save a bit of money by buying your full access ticket online ahead of your visit! 
.
EAT:
🍴 There are tons of food options in Blue Mountain Village. We enjoyed Sunset Grill for breakfast, Northwinds Brewery for lunch and sitting on the beautiful patio at Firehall Pizza for dinner! 
.
What questions do you have?! We’re happy to share any other details of our stay that you’re interested in! 
.
#bluemtnresort #summerstaybluemtn

caption:
Ontario Road Trip idea with kids! ⭐️ SAVE for LATER ⭐️ 
.
Start in the GTA and take the approximately 2.5 hour drive out to beautiful Muskoka, aka ‘Cottage Country’.
.
Here are the stops we recommend for kids on this route:
.
📍 Painswick Park in Barrie: Play at the huge accessible playground, and have a picnic under the covered gazebos. Unfortunately there are no bathrooms on site, but there are porta-potties.
.
 📍 Walter Henry Park in Orillia: Another huge and gorgeous playground to let kids run off some energy! This park features a double zipline, large climbing structure, and a human-built creek for water play. 
.
📍 Muskoka Discovery Centre in Gravenhurst: Learn about the Muskoka region through tons of play-based activities. This stop is indoors so it’s great for rainy days or just to get a break from the sun. It’s on the waterfront so also has beautiful views. 
.
📍Boston Pizza in Gravenhurst: Located just a few minutes walk from the Discovery Centre & right on the waterfront, this is a great lunch or dinner stop! 
.
📍 Santa’s Village in Bracebridge: There is so much to do at Santa’s Village, it’s a destination all on its own, so plan to spend at least half a day here! Go to Elf School, ride the train & rides and play at the splash pad! 
.
📍 High Falls in Bracebridge: This is a beautiful nature spot and one of the biggest waterfalls in the region. It’s definitely worth a visit, but make sure to keep kids close as you explore! 
.
📍 Hunters Bay Trail, Huntsville: Huntsville is a great place to use as home-base while exploring Muskoka. It’s an easy drive to multiple provincial parks and tons of gorgeous lakes and trails. Our favourite activity in Huntsville itself is the beautiful floating boardwalk of Hunters Bay Trail! 
.
📍 Algonquin Outfitters on Oxtongue Lake: No trip to Muskoka is complete without getting out on the water Rent a canoe or kayak at Algonquin Outfitters and explore Oxtongue Lake. 
.

📌SAVE for Ontario Family Staycation Inspiration!
.
Midland and Penetanguishene, located about 2 hours north of Toronto, are home to beautiful parks, attractions and beaches your family will love!
.
Here’s a quick weekend itinerary that’s great for kids:

Day 1
📍 McGuire Park
Drive to Midland and Penetanguishene and take the kids to this big epic playground to blow off some energy!
.
📍 Discovery Harbour @discoveryharbour 
Spend the morning immersing in Canadian History! Explore replica ships, and a historical village, chat with costumed interpreters and learn to clean a cannon or use woodworking tools!
.
📍 Maple Canadian Pub @maplecanadianpub 
Eat dinner on a waterfront patio with a beautiful view of the Marina and Midland Bay.
.
📍 Hampton Inn by Hilton Midland @hamptoninnmidland 
Check into your hotel and head to the pool for a swim before bed!
.
Day 2
📍 Awenda Provincial Park @awenda_pp 
Pack a lunch and plan to spend the whole day here as there is plenty to do. Three activities that are great for kids:
1. Walk the Beaver Pond boardwalk trail, which is less than 1 km but passes over several creeks and is great fun for kids!
2. Hit the beach! We walked the path to Beach 3, which is a bit rocky but the views are lovely 
3. Canoe on Kettle’s Lake! Canoe rentals are available & they provide everything you need! The lake is quite small, making it manageable for beginners and young families to paddle. 
.
📍 Woodland Beach in Tiny. Another great beach to visit on the way home!

.

Start your morning with a visit to our second favourite playground in the city - Grange Park ! This playground is a beautiful & is also located right beside the Art Gallery of Ontario. .
Day 4: Toronto Zoo & Splash Island
Head to the north end of the city to visit the huge Toronto zoo. Here you can ride the Zoomobile, see thousands of animals, and visit ‘Splash Island’ - the huge Canada themed splash pad!

DETAILS 👇 
.
SAVE this for future adventure inspiration!
.
This beautiful hike is the Grassi Lakes Trail, located approximately 1 hour from Calgary and 20 minutes from Banff, Alberta! 
.
The gorgeous blue-green lakes are a great reward at the end of the 2km (total 4 km out and back) hike. We packed treats for the kids to enjoy once we reached the lakes, which was a great motivator!
.
There are two routes to get to the lakes. Just passed the trailhead you can choose between the more challenging route (head left) or the easier, big jogger/trail-stroller-friendly route (stay right). If you are able to take the more challenging route, you’ll be rewarded with beautiful views of Quarry Lake & Canmore below and a stunning waterfall! 
.
We chose to hike up along the more challenging route, enjoy some treats as we explored the Grassi Lakes at the top, and then head down the easier route when the kids were running out of steam!
.
‼️ Note that Grassi Lakes is a very popular trail (for good reason!) so it’s best to visit on a weekday and early morning if possible! 
.
.
.

caption:
DETAILS 👇 
.
We recently visited Niagara Falls on the Ontario/Canada side and packed our quick 2 day, 1 night visit full of fun. This is the kid-friendly itinerary we followed…
.
Day 1
📍Butterfly Conservatory: We started our trip with a stop at the Butterfly Conservatory where we were surrounded by beautiful butterflies and even had them land on us! There’s also a cafe here for lunch! 
.
📍 Horseshoe Falls: We walked the pathway along the falls and watched the boats down below 
.
📍 Clifton Hill and the Niagara SkyWheel: Next we walked up to Clifton Hill and the Niagara SkyWheel. There is tons to do here including arcades, rides and mini putt.
.
📍 Skylon Tower Revolving Restaurant: We had dinner here and it was such a cool and unique way to see the falls. The restaurant rotates about once every hour. Your ride up to the top of tower is complementary when you go for lunch or dinner. 
.
📍 Fairfield Inn by Marriott: We checked in at our hotel and went for a swim in the pool. Breakfast is also included here and we went for another swim before heading out the next morning. 
.
Day 2
📍 White Water Walk: We arrived at 9:00 am right when this attraction opened and took the elevator down into the gorge. Then walked the 400m boardwalk alongside the class 6 rapids on the Niagara River. This is a very easy walk that took us about 20-30 minutes.
.
📍 Safari Niagara: Next we drive about 20 minutes to Safari Niagara where you can easily spend the day. We fed the giraffes and rhino, saw a baby hippo and played at the huge splash pad!
.
.
.
Questions?!
.
.
